The CF accounts for availability, outages, reliability, maintenance, operation at a reduced capacity, and other times when the plant may not be operating. The overall CF of the plant was assumed to be 90 percent, which is consistent with commercial SMR plants that produce hydrogen, assuming a single reactor operating at full capacity (Lewis, et al., 2022). The implementation of carbon capture and ammonia production was assumed not to impact the CF. 2.6 WATER USE A water balance was performed on the major water consumers in the process. The water demand, representing the total amount of water required for a particular process for each subsystem, was determined and internal recycle water recovered from various sources, such as condensate from syngas, was applied to offset the water demand. The difference between demand and recycle is raw water withdrawal. Raw water withdrawal is defined as the water removed from the ground or diverted from a publicly owned treatment works (POTW) for use in the plant for all purposes, such as steam production and cooling tower makeup. In this study, raw water was assumed to be provided 50 percent by a POTW and 50 percent from groundwater. The difference between water withdrawal and process water discharge is defined as raw water consumption, which is also accounted for as the portion of the raw water withdrawn that is evaporated, transpired, incorporated into products, or otherwise not returned to the water source from which it was withdrawn. Consumption represents the net impact of the process on the water source. The water balances presented in subsequent sections include the water demand of the major water consumers within the process, the amount provided by internal recycle, the amount of raw water withdrawal by difference, the amount of process water returned to the source, and the raw water consumption, again by difference. 22 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION 2.7 ENVIRONMENTAL TARGETS 2.7.1 Air Emissions Targets Air emissions targets for the ammonia study cases align with targets established for natural gas combined cycle (NGCC) (Turner, et al., 2025).
